GERMAN — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #18
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: GERMAN
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. German for “school” is: (1 mark)
   A. Buch
   B. Haus
   C. Schule
   D. Wasser

2. When practising Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading.

3. When practising Writing 1.3.1: Descriptive writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.3.1: Descriptive writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.3.1: Descriptive writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.3.1: Descriptive writing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.3.1: Descriptive writing.

4. When practising Grammar, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar.

5. When practising Grammar 1.4.1 Verbs and Pronouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar 1.4.1 Verbs and Pronouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar 1.4.1 Verbs and Pronouns.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar 1.4.1 Verbs and Pronouns.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar 1.4.1 Verbs and Pronouns.

6. “Guten Tag” means: (1 mark)
   A. Good day / hello
   B. Please
   C. Thank you
   D. Good night

7. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Conversational skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Conversational skills.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Conversational skills.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Conversational skills.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Conversational skills.

8. When practising Writing 2.3.2 Descriptive writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.3.2 Descriptive writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.3.2 Descriptive writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.3.2 Descriptive writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.3.2 Descriptive writing.

9. When practising Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing.

10. When practising Reading 1.2.2 Reading Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.2 Reading Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.2 Reading Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.2 Reading Comprehension.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.2 Reading Comprehension.

11. When practising Reading 2.2.2 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.2 Intensive Reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.2 Intensive Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.2 Intensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.2 Intensive Reading.

12. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Dialogic Skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Dialogic Skills.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Dialogic Skills.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Dialogic Skills.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Dialogic Skills.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 4.2.2 Reading for Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 4.3.3: Functional writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar 4.4.4 Accusative and Dative Case ● Definite, indefinite and negative art and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Schule

2. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading.

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.3.1: Descriptive writing.

4. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar.

5. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar 1.4.1 Verbs and Pronouns.

6. A — Good day / hello

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Conversational skills.

8. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.3.2 Descriptive writing.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing.

10. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.2 Reading Comprehension.

11. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.2 Intensive Reading.

12. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Dialogic Skills.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 4.2.2 Reading for Comprehension; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 4.3.3: Functional writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar 4.4.4 Accusative and Dative Case ● Definite, indefinite and negative art; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 5.1.1; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
